memory_candidates.content: In this repo, a full (non-`--skip-slow`) `verify-deploy.sh` battery run reliably exceeds a 540s bounded-wait inner timeout inside gate 8's shell-test-suite runner (observed twice, consistently). When a plan's verification step needs a full-battery comparison against a baseline, pre-declare a `--skip-slow` fallback contingency (same mode on both sides of the comparison) rather than assuming the plain full run will complete within 540s.

`generate-context-line-counts.sh --write` recomputes `line_count` for EVERY entry in EVERY extension's source `index-entries.json` in one pass -- it is not scoped to the file you intend to fix. On a shared, actively multi-tasked working tree, a `--write` run can silently fold in corrections for entries that drifted due to concurrent sibling-task edits landing between a `--check` and a `--write` invocation. Diff the result before committing; hand-revert (via `sed` on the specific line) any entry outside your own task's `file_scope` rather than trusting the bulk write wholesale.

A verify-deploy.sh test fixture whose `.claude` directory is a SYMLINK to the real, shared deployed tree (used by test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh and similar suites, for speed) inherits that tree's ambient deploy-staleness and content-drift noise from concurrently-landing sibling tasks' edits -- a full-battery baseline-sanity assertion inside such a fixture can fail for reasons entirely unrelated to the gate under test. Before concluding a new gate is broken, reproduce the fixture standalone and run the new gate in isolation (`--only-gate N`) against it to separate gate-under-test correctness from ambient tree staleness.
